checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are largely accurate but slightly lenient on the 'V-shaped snout' checkpoint. While the snout is visible, the resolution and water distortion make a definitive 'V vs U' distinction difficult; however, it is certainly not an alligator-like U-shape, so 'Present' is acceptable. The Router correctly marked teeth and ventral scales as untestable due to occlusion/submersion. The limb digit count was also correctly marked untestable. No checkpoints were incorrectly skipped.
artifact_review: The Router identified texture anomalies in the water reflection (severity 1.5) and boundary bleeding (severity 1.0). These are valid observations. The Perceptual Quality Auditor noted slight compression artifacts (severity 0.2), which aligns with the visual evidence of a somewhat soft, low-resolution image. The Animal Pose Auditor found low confidence in facial keypoints, which correlates with the difficulty of resolving fine facial features in this lighting/resolution, but did not flag structural limb errors. The Topology Auditor confirmed a coherent mask. I agree with the Router's artifact severity assessments; the water reflection is the most significant tell-tale sign of AI generation here, appearing overly smooth and lacking complex refraction physics.
alignment_reasoning: The Fine Grained Classifier strongly confirms the class as 'African crocodile' (Logit 7.44 vs 4.6 for Alligator), providing high confidence in species alignment. Visually, the scute pattern, body proportions, and head shape match the taxonomy. 7 out of 10 checkpoints were testable and passed. The 3 untestable checkpoints were legitimately occluded. The image conforms well to the class definition despite minor resolution limitations.
artifact_reasoning: The primary artifact is the unnatural water reflection/refraction around the body, which appears as a simple blur rather than complex optical distortion (Severity ~1.5). There is minor boundary softness where the limbs meet the water/mud. The image has slight compression noise. No catastrophic structural failures (melting, extra limbs) were detected by experts or visually observed. The score reflects a good quality generation with subtle physical inconsistencies in the environment interaction.
